Overview¶

The goal of the final project is for you to create a digital analytical edition of a corpus using the tools, practices, and perspectives you’ve learning in this course. You will select a corpus that has already been digitized and transcribed, parse that into an F-compliant set of tables, and then generate and visualize the results of a series of fitted models. You will also draw some tentative conclusions regarding the linguistic, cultural, psychological, or historical features represented by your corpus. The point of the exercise is to have you work with a corpus through the entire pipeline from ingestion to interpretation.

Specifically, you will acquire a collection of long-form texts and perform the following operations:

  • Convert the collection from their source formats (F0) into a set of tables that conform to the Standard Text Analytic Data Model (F2).
  • Annotate these tables with statistical and linguistic features using NLP libraries such as NLTK (F3).
  • Produce a vector representation of the corpus to generate TFIDF values to add to the TOKEN (aka CORPUS) and VOCAB tables (F4).
  • Model the annotated and vectorized model with tables and features derived from the application of unsupervised methods, including PCA, LDA, and word2vec (F5).
  • Explore your results using statistical and visual methods.
  • Present conclusions about patterns observed in the corpus by means of these operations.

When you are finished, you will make the results of your work available in GitHub (for code) and UVA Box (for data). You will submit to Gradescope (via Canvas) a PDF version of a Jupyter notebook that contains the information listed below.

Source Document Structure (1)¶

Provide a brief description of the internal structure of each document. That, describe the typical elements found in document and their relation to each other. For example, a corpus of letters might be described as having a date, an addressee, a salutation, a set of content paragraphs, and closing. If they are various structures, state that.

The document's columns include a unique identifier (id), the season number, episode number, scene number. It also contains the line text, which sometimes can contain other details about how the line was spoken (ex: [on the phone], [singing], [Dwight begins smashing pencils with his phone]). It also notes the speaker and whether or not the line was deleted, which is a boolean value.

Riff 1 (5)¶

(INSERT IMAGE HERE)

(INSERT INTERPRETATION HERE)

I decided to look more into topic 2, which was the one that had to do with partying and social events, and I looked into the peaks of that topic in this line plot. Season 2, episode 13 was the first peak, which is the episode where Jim has a crush on Pam and they go to Hooters, which makes sense. The tall peak far on the right is S9E9, where Dwight plans a christmas party (makes sense again), and the tall peak in the middle is about some of the people being in Florida while Andy has to cover for them.

Riff 2 (5)¶

(INSERT IMAGE HERE) (INSERT INTERPRETATION HERE)

I decided to look more into each of the more prominent characters in the show, Michael, Jim, Pam, and Dwight, to see which characters were most prominently involved in each of the topics. It's clear with all of the blue that Michael is involved in nearly everything and is the most prominent person in all of the topics. This was calculated by using the top words and counting the number of times each top word was said by each person. Some things that stood out to me were that T1 (having a lot to do with phones and calling clients), Dwight and Jim were very high on these whereas Pam wasn't, which makes sense as she is a receptionist as opposed to a salesperson. You can also see that T0 is higher from Dwight and Jim (has to do with playfulness and fighting), as the two frequently "fight" each other in the show.

Riff 3 (5)¶

(INSERT IMAGE HERE) (INSERT INTERPRETATION HERE) I decided to see which characters are most similar to each other, and unsurprisingly Jim and Pam are very similar to each other, I think it's notable that Michael is the most dissimilar to everyone on the plot. I find it odd that Karen and Creed are the most similar, when I don't think they really interact at all in the show. It could possibly be that both of them, as well as Kelly and Jan aren't really large parts of the show. All of them have episodes where they're relevant but I wouldn't call any of them main characters. It is notable to me that Andy isn't closer to Jim or Dwight, especially since all of them are the big salesmen you think of in the show.

Interpretation (4)¶

Describe something interesting about your corpus that you discovered during the process of completing this assignment.

At a minumum, use 250 words, but you may use more. You may also add images if you'd like.

(INSERT INTERPRETATION HERE) I think it was interesting to learn that some of the characters that weren't similar at all from watching the show turn out to be very similar when you analyze it. Noting that Kelly and Karen and Creed were all similar was strange to me. I can see how Kelly and Karen are similar as they both had very strange relationships with Jim, where Karen and Jim dated but Kelly often was romantically involved with Ryan. Phyllis, Kevin and Angela in the same area makes a lot of sense as they all seem to be a bit older and they all are in the same area of the office generally. In some ways though they all have very different personalities, with Kevin being very silly and Angela being very serious, which makes the graph look a little bit strange. It's interesting to see how you can use the topics to find an episode you want to watch. For example, I was looking at T10 and there are lots of words like warehouse, pizza, union, men, and the highest episode is Season 2 Episode 15, where Michael has his seminar in response to the Women in the Workplace seminar and hosts it with the men in the warehouse.

I also looked into T7, where the top terms were spot, scranton, montage, clip, and the top episode is Season 6, Episode 13, which is the Santa episode. I'm not sure if this is accurate, as I can't remember them showing any clips or montages in this episode, but there could be more I didn't consider. Overall, I thought this was a really interesting assignment and a way to further understand the script and how much nuance there is in the show.
